stem: Choose the articles matching standard pronunciation: “The guide took ___ umbrella and ___ uniform from the locker.”

choices.text: a; an
an; an
an; a
a; a

explanation: Umbrella begins with a vowel sound, requiring an; uniform begins with the consonant /y/ sound, requiring a. The written initial u does not determine both articles.

stem: Choose the pronoun required after the preposition: “The remaining supplies are for Liza and ___.”

choices.text: I
my
mine
me

explanation: The preposition for takes an object form: me. I is a subject form, while my/mine are possessives and do not fill this coordinated personal-object slot.

stem: Choose the form that completes the sentence: “To protect the wet ink, avoid ___ the printed surface.”

choices.text: touching
to touch
touch
touched

explanation: When avoid is followed by a verb, the -ing form is used: avoid touching. The infinitive, bare form and past form do not fit this construction.

stem: Intended meaning: the bell rang, and as a result the audience stood. Choose the revision that keeps that relation and avoids joining two independent clauses with only a comma.

choices.text: The bell rang, the audience stood.
The bell rang, so the audience stood.
Because the audience stood, the bell rang.
The bell rang although the audience stood.

explanation: So joins the independent clauses and expresses the intended result. A comma alone creates a splice; because reverses cause and effect, while although introduces a concession not intended here.

stem: Mila formerly worked at night but now works days. Neri still works at night and finds that schedule familiar. Which pair preserves these different meanings in standard English?

choices.text: Mila is used to working nights; Neri used to work nights.
Mila used to working nights; Neri is used to work nights.
Mila used to work nights; Neri is used to working nights.
Mila is used to work nights; Neri used to working nights.

explanation: Used to plus a base verb describes the former habit; is used to plus an -ing form describes present familiarity. Reversing the constructions swaps the intended states; the other combinations use incompatible forms.

stem: The intended relation is that work continued in spite of the heavy rain. Which sentence expresses that relation with a complete grammatical construction?

choices.text: Despite the rain was heavy, work continued.
Although the heavy rain, work continued.
Because of the heavy rain, work continued.
Despite the heavy rain, work continued.

explanation: Despite takes the noun phrase the heavy rain; although would need a clause such as although the rain was heavy. Because of is grammatical with a noun phrase but changes concession to cause.

stem: The original statement is “The old lift seldom stops between floors.” Which formal revision begins with SELDOM, uses standard inversion and preserves the frequency?

choices.text: Seldom does the old lift stop between floors.
Seldom the old lift does stop between floors.
Seldom does the old lift stops between floors.
Seldom does the old lift never stop between floors.

explanation: Fronted negative-frequency seldom calls for auxiliary-subject inversion, with does plus base stop. Retaining ordinary order or adding -s after does is faulty; adding never changes the frequency meaning.
